analysis.title: Month-End Perspective: US Pension Rebalancing, $9 billion to sell as fixed income outperformed equities
key_insights: GS desk model estimates US pensions will sell $9bn of US equities into month-end and buy an equivalent amount of bonds, driven by fixed income outperforming equities.
The rebalance estimate peaked at $20bn to sell until the vol market flinch on Oct 16, then declined into single digits. It has ranged $7-9bn since last Friday and sits at $9bn.

$9bn to sell is the 50th percentile in absolute dollar terms over three years and the 65th percentile since Jan 2000. On a net basis it is the 39th percentile over three years and the 22nd since Jan 2000.
MTD, fixed income outperformed US equities by 1.98%: S&P total return 0.39% vs 10yr total return 2.37%.

October brought widespread investor pain, culminating in a vol flinch midway through the month. The S&P fell less than 50bps last week and is 1.1% below its highs, but hedge fund portfolios took heavy losses underneath.
Last Thursday, Fundamental L/S, Systematic and Multi-Strat funds each lost more than 1% on the same day, the first time since COVID.
The GS Risk Appetite Indicator posted one of its largest declines on record and is at its lowest level since April 2025.
On Oct 16 VIX futures were aggressively bought and VIX spiked to its highest level since July. VVIX rose 17 points, one of the largest 1-day moves in four years. Vol has not fully reset.
The GS Vol Panic Index jumped 3 points Wednesday and reached nearly 8/10 on Friday, essentially at the 'panic' threshold for the first time since late July.
S&P spot is chopping around its 50-day moving average, with most dealer long gamma to the topside. Skew collapsed coming out of the weekend and spot vol compressed with yesterday's rally.
NDX vol underperformed significantly despite tech-led spot outperformance, which highlights the steep NDX-S&P vol spread.
Upcoming catalysts are earnings from 44% of S&P market cap, FOMC tomorrow, and elections. The desk thinks short-dated limited-loss structures remain the best way to play them.
Desk flow has been generally quiet, with some traction in single stocks. The desk likes Mag7 upside, specifically AMZN 18Dec'26 call spreads.
CTA positioning is beginning to moderate after last week's top-percentile selling. The 5-day change in S&P and NDX positioning is the largest drop since April.
